text:
support-jan: :rotating_light: Customer-tier alert from acct_4321 — sustained 502/504s and elevated p99 latency hitting hosted inference in eastus2 AZ3 since ~08:05 UTC. Multiple customers reporting timeouts and partial responses. Raising here for triage.

devon: seeing the same in our dashboards — spike in gateway 502s from az3 to model-proxy group. 5xx rate ~13% for the last 10m.

ops-bot: Alert: gateway-502-rate high (eastus2/az3) — 13% 5xx — triggered at 2026-03-15T08:07:12Z.

maria: @devon can you paste a sample error payload? need to know if it's upstream 502 from model process or our edge gateway.

devon: paste logs from edge (redacted):
```
[08:06:59] gateway: request_id=abc123 status=502 backend_err="upstream reset" path=/v1/infer model=redwood-3b
[08:07:03] gateway: request_id=abc124 status=502 backend_err="connect timeout" path=/v1/infer model=llama-13b
```

lee: I just rolled a quick check on node pool for az3 — nodes look healthy from K8s perspective, pods Ready. No recent deploys in the last hour.

alex: customer repro steps from support ticket: Samira, can you paste what you have?

samira: Customer says: reproduce with 50 concurrent requests using their prompt set (shared link) — they see ~20% 502 after ~2 minutes. They ran `curl` to our gateway with auth and example: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d @batch.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/infer`

billing: customer also reported abnormal token accounting — some requests returned 502 but were still billed. We need to capture exact request IDs to audit.

maria: running `mtr`/`traceroute` to the node VIP from our control plane in the same region to see packet loss pattern. Will share results.

maria: traceroute output:
```
traceroute to az3-vip (10.2.3.14), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.3 ms
 2  52.114.22.1  1.2 ms
 3  52.114.22.9  1.9 ms
 4  198.51.100.45  5.1 ms  <-- 10% packet loss on this hop
 5  10.2.3.14  5.8 ms
```

devon: that intermediate hop with packet loss aligns with the timing of the 502s. @netops can you check transit/provider side for microbursts or route flaps?

netops: opening ticket with our transit partner now. Provider acknowledges increased retransmits on the eastus2-peering and is investigating BGP flap history. Ticket REF: TP-99821.

sre-lead: mitigation plan: 1) divert new traffic away from AZ3 for customer-tier and critical routes (failover policy) 2) spin up additional endpoints in eastus2/az1 and register as preferred for canary 3) collect pcap from affected gateway to hand to provider 4) preserve logs for billing audit.

devon: I'm enabling canary routing in the routing policy for the affected customers to send 80% to az1 and 20% to az3 for now (to monitor success). Applying k8s Service annotation to prefer healthy endpoints.

ops-bot: Config change: route-policy updated for acct_4321 -> canary (az1 preferred).

samira: letting the customer know we've routed their traffic to a healthy AZ and asked them to retry. They've asked for repro steps to reproduce the failure condition; I gave them the same 50 concurrency script and asked for request_ids when they hit 502.

lee: collecting pcap from the gateway pod with `tcpdump -w /tmp/eastus2_az3.pcap host 10.2.3.14 and port 443` — will upload to internal bucket.

maria: also pulled ENI/TRF counters and seeing bursts of 2-4% packet loss concentrated in 08:05-08:12 window, repeated microbursts. Looks like a carrier-level microburst causing retransmits and connection resets.

netops: provider update: they saw short AS path changes (BGP update storms) around the same time, plus interface errors on one of their aggregator peers. They rerouted traffic and are rolling a fix. Requesting pcap to correlate.

devon: after enabling canary away from az3, 5xx rate for impacted customer dropped to ~0.7% and p99 latency returned to normal. Canary looks good. :thumbsup:

billing: captured list of request IDs that returned 502 in the window; marking them for refund audit. We'll follow up with finance and CS.

sre-lead: next actions: (a) netops to get provider RC and confirm root-cause (carrier interface flaps + BGP churn) (b) infra to run controlled soak on az3 once provider confirms fix (c) support to coordinate refunds and customer comms (d) create postmortem if provider confirms external cause.

netops: provider sent initial RCA: buffer overflow on aggregator interface caused microbursts + BGP updates. They applied IOS patch and stability fixes. Monitoring shows stabilization.

alex: advise we keep failover policy in place for 2h then gradually shift traffic back to az3 with a canary. Coordinate with netops and devon.

samira: customer acknowledged and is running another test now. They report 0/200 502s after failover. Thanks team.

maria: uploading pcap and flow logs to internal bucket: gs://redwood-diagnostics/eastus2/2234567890/pktcap.pcap and linking ticket.

devon: leaving this thread open until provider confirms clean BGP state for 24h. Will update.

support-jan: adding notes to the support ticket and flagging for billing follow-up. Good runbook for this one — provider microbursts -> upstream resets -> gateway 502s -> customer impact -> canary failover worked.

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated (traffic routed) — monitoring.

sre-lead: Assigning postmortem owner @maria. Please include timeline, mitigations, provider RCA, and billing reconciliation steps.

devon: thanks — keeping eyes on dashboards. :eyes:
